seed_error.description:
Why this instance's seed import was refused, if it was.

`None` on every healthy instance — including one that never had a seed
bundle to import. A sandbox whose seed was refused boots with an empty
site and no other sign of it (`dev_runtime::install` logs and carries
on, because a sandbox that refuses to boot is one whose `/b/dev` page
— the only thing that could fix it — never comes up), so this is what
makes the cause readable through `dev_status` instead of only through
the service worker's console. Read from the same row an admin sees on
`/b/admin/settings/variables`, which is the only surface an exported
site has (it has no `/b/dev`). `dev.js` does not render it: the page
polls this endpoint several times a second, so a log line would need
its own "said this already" state, and the agent that would act on a
refused seed reads `dev_status` rather than the log.

tools.description: Write a workspace file under `site/` or `blocks/<name>/`. Writing under `site/` publishes a new generation immediately, live on the sandbox; writing under `blocks/` only stages source — nothing serves it until the block is compiled and staged.

oneOf.description: `content` is the file's text. The default.
`content` is the file's bytes, standard base64 with padding.

expected_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 you expect the file to have right now, or `null` if you
expect it not to exist yet. A mismatch is a `409` carrying the hash
the file actually has, so a caller that has fallen behind re-reads
instead of silently overwriting an edit it never saw.

Omitting the field means the same as `null` — serde defaults an
absent `Option` to `None`, and `#[serde(default)]` says so in the
source rather than leaving it to a rule the schema does not show. That
is a safe default rather than a lax one: over a file that exists,
"I expect nothing here" is itself a conflict.

tools.description: Scaffold a new backend block from a template (`hello` or `table`) under blocks/<name>/. Compile it with dev_compile_block.

name.description:
The block's short name, e.g. `newsletter`. It becomes the directory
`blocks/<name>/`, the crate name, the block id `site/<name>`, the
route prefix `/b/<name>/` and the collection prefix `site__<name>__`
(a hyphen spelled `_` there). 2 to 32 characters: a lowercase letter
followed by lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, with no doubled
hyphen and no trailing hyphen.

template.description:
Which starting point to write. `hello` is one public `GET` and
nothing else; `table` is a newsletter block with a database table, an
agent tool and two admin reads — start there for anything that stores
data.

oneOf.description: One public `GET` and nothing else — the smallest block that serves.

A newsletter block: a claimed collection, a table created in `init`,
a public write endpoint with an agent tool, and two admin reads.

tools.name: dev_create_block

files.description:
The files that were written, in path order. Read or edit them through
the files API; the block does not serve until it is compiled.

items.description:
One file in the workspace: where it is, which blob holds it, how big it is
and what it is served as.

The same type is what a generation's site manifest is made of — a
generation *is* the workspace's `site/` entries, frozen — so there is one
definition rather than a wire type and a stored type that have to be kept
in step.

content_type.description: Content type the file is served with.

path.description:
Where the file lives. Workspace-relative (`site/index.html`) in the
files API; relative to its area's root (`index.html`) in a
generation's site manifest and in a block's source listing.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's content-addressed blob, hex-encoded.

name.description: The block's short name, as written.

tools.description: Remove a compiled block from the running site and activate the resulting generation. Its source under `blocks/<name>/` is untouched — this only takes the compiled block out of what serves.

name.description:
The block's short name, e.g. `hello` for the block registered as
`site/hello`.

tools.name: dev_remove_block

outputSchema.description: Response of every endpoint whose whole job is to activate a generation.

activated_at.description: RFC 3339 time the generation went live, or null if it never did.

blocks.description: Number of blocks in the generation's block manifest.

oneOf.description: A `site/**` write. Site-only — no runtime rebuild.
A `site/**` delete. Site-only — no runtime rebuild.
A successful compile stage; the block set changed.
A block was removed; the block set changed.
A republish of an earlier generation's manifests.
Generation 0, imported from the seed bundle on cold boot.

parent_id.description: The generation this one was derived from, or null for the first.

site_files.description: Number of files in the generation's site manifest.

status.description: Where the generation sits in its lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Recorded, not yet examined.
Blobs, artifacts and guests are being checked.
The runtime swap and site publish are in progress.
Currently serving.
Abandoned; `failure_message` says why.

No longer serving — replaced by a later generation.

Written by the activation that replaced it, and by nothing else. It is
not an ageing marker: a generation that falls out of the retention
window is deleted rather than relabelled, so a `failed` generation
still reads as `failed` for as long as the ledger keeps it.

progress.description:
One entry per phase the activation passed through, with how long it
took. The last is always `active`.

items.description:
One phase of an activation, with how long it took.

Published in every mutating tool result (design §7.5) so the page can show
where the time went without a push channel.

detail.description: Human-readable detail for the progress panel.

oneOf.description: Nothing in flight.

tools.description: The authoring reference for backend blocks: API, host services, limits, and the two templates. Read it before writing Rust.
tools.name: dev_read_reference

markdown.description:
The authoring guide, as Markdown: the API, the host services, the
namespace rules, the limits, the diagnostic codes, and both templates
in full.

wafer_guest_module.description:
The current `src/wafer_guest.rs`, verbatim: what a block built against
an older copy writes over its own before compiling again.

wafer_guest_version.description:
The `WAFER_GUEST_VERSION` of the support module this reference
documents and `POST /b/dev/api/blocks` writes.

tools.description: What exporting the site right now would produce: every file of the bundle with its size, the totals, and the rows of each data table. A read — use `dev_export` to actually download it.
tools.name: dev_export_manifest

outputSchema.description:
Response of `GET /b/dev/api/export/manifest` — what
`GET /b/dev/api/export` would produce, without producing it.

blocks.description:
How many compiled blocks the export carries. Each contributes its
`.wasm` plus its whole source tree.

files.description: Every entry of the archive, in the order it is written.

items.description:
One entry of the export bundle: where it lands in the zip, and how big it
is.

bytes.description:
The entry's uncompressed size in bytes. The archive stores entries
uncompressed, so this is also what it costs in the zip.

generation_id.description:
The generation the export is a snapshot of — the one that is live now.
The downloaded file is named after its first eight characters.

shell_files.description:
How many of `files` are the runtime shell (the service worker, the
wasm, the loader — everything that makes the folder runnable).

site_files.description: How many are the site's own files, under `seed/site/`.

tables.description:
Rows the data snapshot carries, per table — products, offers,
settings and accounts (`seed/data.json`).

total_bytes.description:
Total size of every entry's content. The archive itself is slightly
larger: each entry carries a local header and a central directory
record naming it.
